text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Paging Aisha (oncall) — Alert: Dedicated pool 'eu-dedicated-42' autoscaler hitting max_nodes, sustained queue growth 5m. Severity: P2.

Aisha: On it. seeing spike in queue length on eu-dedicated-42 and some 503s from the allocator. Is this customer traffic or internal test?

Diego: Looks customer. AcmeCorp spike across multiple regions, ~3x normal. They're on Dedicated but burst_capacity was off this morning after the last maintenance.

Aisha: Ok. Immediate plan: 1) enable burst capacity on pool, 2) temporarily bump max_nodes + apply soft per-tenant throttle for AcmeCorp, 3) disable nonessential features (streaming / long-context) for that tenant if needed, 4) notify account and support.

Sam: +1. How do we enable burst quickly? rwctl command?

Caroline: Use rwctl or the infra console. CLI: `rwctl pools update eu-dedicated-42 --burst true --max-nodes 60` (current max 24). That should allow autoscaler to spawn more until reserved/backfill capacity arrives.

Aisha: Running that now. Pasting command so it's auditable:

```
# enable burst capacity and increase cap
rwctl pools update eu-dedicated-42 --set burst_capacity=true --set max_nodes=60 --reason "emergency surge: AcmeCorp"
```

Aisha: Command submitted. Waiting for confirmation from control plane.

IncidentBot: Action accepted: pool update queued. ETA for nodes ~90s per node launch; provisioning ramp expected ~5-7m for +36 nodes.

Ben: While nodes spin up we should apply soft quota/rate-limit on AcmeCorp to reduce error rate. I can apply a per-tenant token_rate_limit via the routing policy. Suggest 60% of their recent burst for 5m sliding window.

Diego: Agreed. Ben, go ahead. Use the routing API: POST /admin/routing/tenants/AcmeCorp/limits with JSON. Example: `{ "rate_per_min": 30000, "window_sec": 300, "soft": true }`.

Ben: Applying now. Payload below: 

```
POST https://admin.redwood.local/admin/routing/tenants/AcmeCorp/limits
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

{
  "rate_per_min": 30000,
  "window_sec": 300,
  "soft": true,
  "note": "Emergency soft throttle during autoscale"
}
```

Ben: API returned 202 accepted. Policy id: rp-2026-557.

Caroline: Also toggle feature flags for that tenant to reduce load. `ffctl set AcmeCorp::enable_streaming false` and `ffctl set AcmeCorp::long_context false` — that'll reduce token churn and KV cache pressure.

Aisha: I'm going to set those flags now.

```
ffctl set AcmeCorp::enable_streaming false --actor=Aisha --reason="mitigation for surge"
ffctl set AcmeCorp::long_context false --actor=Aisha --reason="mitigation for surge"
```

Aisha: Flags applied. Support note: Caro, can you ping the account team to let them know we're applying temporary throttles and feature changes? We'll rollback when stable.

Caroline: On it. Messaging ACME account slack and opening a support thread. Draft note: "We're seeing a traffic surge on your Dedicated pool; to ensure stability we've temporarily enabled burst capacity and applied a soft rate limit plus disabled streaming/long-context. We expect recovery within ~10 mins; please advise if you have critical jobs in flight."

Sam: Monitoring logs — 503s dropped from 14% -> 6% since throttle applied. Node provisioning still ramping. KV cache miss rate trending down after flags.

Diego: Good. Any customer-facing impact besides degraded streaming? Need to call out in incident.

Aisha: Yes: short interruptions to streaming sessions and increased latency for long-context calls; text generation (non-stream) largely ok but slower. No data loss. Severity: P2, targeted to AcmeCorp only since we throttled tenant routing.

Ben: Autoscaler update: current nodes 24 -> provisioning 36 -> will cap at 60. Keep an eye on backoff signs (OOM / RT spikes) — if we hit other limits we should revert and route to hosted fallback.

Aisha: Agree. Prepare fallback plan if health deteriorates: 1) mark pool draining for non-critical routes, 2) route eligible calls to hosted model variants (smaller model) via policy `route_fallback=hosted-small`, 3) engage capacity team for long-term adjustments.

Caroline: Support ticket created (#INC-2026-331) and customer notified. Copying internal note to thread.

Aisha: Update: nodes active increased to 42 now. Queue length falling ~60%. 503s down to 2.1%. Sam, any anomalies in autoscaler logs?

Sam: Logs show successful launches, but one node had a failed health probe then recovered. Nothing systemic.

Diego: Recommend we leave burst on for another 15m and monitor. If stable, incrementally reduce soft throttles and re-enable streaming/long-context for AcmeCorp.

Aisha: Agree. I'll hand this to Ben for 15m watch then to the next oncall (Ben -> Diego handoff). Ben, please post status update at +15.

Ben: Will do. Handoff note: AcmeCorp surge mitigated by burst + soft throttle + feature flags; autoscaler scaled to 42/60; monitor for regressions; support notified. Taking watch.

IncidentBot: Handoff recorded. Next oncall: Diego at 1905302250.

Ben: Quick follow-ups for postmortem: 1) why burst_capacity was toggled off earlier today? 2) consider automated burst enable rule when queue growth > X for reserved customers, 3) validate throttle automation and feature-flag rollback sequence. I'll draft RCA template.

Aisha: Thanks team. Good job moving fast. I'll join the RCA doc after stable. :thumbsup:

Diego: +1. Closing thread if no more alerts.

Ben: Still watching; will update at +15.

(--- end of thread ---)
